answer: The island escrow holds each stake, the tundra settlement releases it, and the thread audit lists every transfer. An identity that attests to another stakes 9% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. A farm running 118 keys as a result pays that exposure 118 times over before it earns anything, as its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
